score.moat_justification: Weak moat: a technology-led ACA exchange insurer whose genuine edge is administrative cost — SG&A ratio fell from 19.1% of revenue (FY2024) to 17.5% (FY2025) to a guided 15.6–16.1% for FY2026, with a record-low 14.2% in Q2 2026 — plus scale as one of the largest pure-play exchange carriers (2.96M members at 2026-06-30, +46% YoY). description.text: Oscar is a leading healthcare technology company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on member experience. We offer health plans through the ACA serving individuals, families, and employees. We have been challenging the status quo in the healthcare system since our founding in 2012 and are dedicated to making a healthier life accessible and affordable for all. Our technology drives superior experiences, deep engagement, and high-value clinical care, earning us the trust of approximately 2.0 million effectuated members, as of December 31, 2025. Effectuated members are those who are actively enrolled in our plan and have either paid their premium or are within the grace period. In addition to supporting our insurance business, our differentiated technology platform also powers both providers and payors through +Oscar. We offer Campaign Builder, an engagement and recommendation platform that leverages the wisdom from 13+ years of building the Oscar member experience. The platform leverages data and AI to identify high value opportunities for engagement and to deliver personalized interactions to improve care with real time reporting and analytics to measure key outcomes and insights. In 2025, we also acquired early-stage businesses with capabilities to help us power Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangements (“ICHRA”) and further diversify the Company.

Oscar Health serves millions of consumers, employers, brokers, and partners through Oscar Insurance, Lucie Health Marketplace, and Trove Group. Together these businesses deliver exceptional lifestyle products and technology platforms that make healthcare easy to choose, use, and experience.

analysis_md:
# OSCR — Oscar Health, Inc.
Engine 5.4 pass-1 run, 2026-10-19. Market cap $8.488B at $32.35 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B. SIC 6324 (Hospital & Medical Service Plans): an ACA health insurer filed under Health Care, which matters for the model-fit verdict below.

All figures are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. Guidance and MLR detail are from the company's FY2025 10-K results and its September 16, 2026 8-K guidance update, as cited.

## What it is
Technology-led health insurer selling ACA individual and small-group plans (2,042,449 members at 2025-12-31; 2.96M at 2026-06-30, +46% YoY), plus ICHRA offerings and the +Oscar platform. Essentially a single-line insurer: premiums were $11,469,893,000 of FY2025 total revenue of $11,701,427,000 (10-K), the rest investment and other income.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,094,854,000; capex $36,372,000; SBC $87,654,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $970,828,000 = $3.70/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share $3.699971035260759), against a **net loss of −$443,151,000** and an operating loss of −$396,357,000 for the same year. That gap is the whole story of this run — see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE below.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $434,937,000 — also far above earnings, because ΔNWC was −$878,088,000 (liabilities — claims payable, risk-adjustment payable, unearned premiums — grew with the member base). For an insurer, both OCF-based definitions capitalize float.
- OE positive 3 of the last 5 fiscal years on the conservative definition; on an earnings basis the company lost money in 2019–2023 and FY2025.
- Real revenue (filer total, fundamentals.json — the engine's contract-revenue tag captures only the $28,593,000 "other revenues" sliver, see BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT): $5,862,869,000 (2023, +47.9%), $9,177,564,000 (2024, +56.5%), $11,701,427,000 (2025, +27.5%), TTM to 2026-06-30 $15,318,633,000 (+42.8% YoY). FY2026 revenue guidance held at $18.7–19.0B (September 16, 2026 8-K).
- SBC trend (DILUTION resolution input): $159,683,000 (2023) → $109,824,000 (2024) → $87,654,000 (2025) → $75,193,000 TTM — falling in dollars while revenue roughly doubled. SBC is not the dilution problem here; the share-count basis is (see DILUTION).

**Base used = the engine's normalized base: median of last-3-FY conservative OE/share = $3.1614162713981036** (2023 −$2.06, 2024 $3.16, 2025 $3.70 per financials_history.csv), base_source `median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share`. It is used as the engine headline but NOT trusted as distributable earnings — the tier is notched for exactly that (see verdict).

**TTM rejected as the base.** ttm.py (through 2026-06-30) prints TTM OCF $4,418,570,000 − capex $38,625,000 − SBC $75,193,000 = TTM OE $4,304,752,000 = $12.99383021624428/share on 331,292,000 diluted shares. The legs show why: current-YTD (H1 2026) OCF alone was $4,711,325,000 against FY2025's full-year $1,094,854,000 — ACA premiums are collected front-loaded in H1 while claims season into H2 (Q3 2025 OCF was −$964,658,000, fundamentals.json quarterly), and a +46% membership surge mechanically inflates premium float. TTM net income over the same window is $550,743,000 and TTM operating income $629,723,000 (fundamentals.json) — TTM "OE" is ~7.8× TTM net income. Annualizing H1 insurer cash flow would be the RNR/PFG float error at full size, so the FY-median base stands and the TTM is reported, not used.

**The 2026 inflection is real, and it is in the earnings, not just the float:** Q1 2026 net income $678,996,000 and Q2 2026 $361,808,000 (fundamentals.json quarterly), MLR guided down to 81–82% for FY2026 with operating-earnings guidance raised to $600–800M (September 16, 2026 8-K) — but the same guidance implies a losing H2 (H1 operating earnings ~$1.09B per the Q2 report), Q2 included $164M of favorable prior-period reserve development, and FY2025's MLR was 87.4% (10-K) after risk-adjustment true-ups. Earnings power is genuinely improving; it is not yet proven through a full cycle.

## Moat: 3/10 — weak
Justification: administrative-cost edge and exchange scale, but no pricing power, no switching costs, a structural risk-adjustment tax on its member mix, and no through-cycle earnings record.
- FOR: proprietary tech/AI platform driving the SG&A ratio from 19.1% (FY2024) to 17.5% (FY2025), guided 15.6–16.1% FY2026, record-low 14.2% in Q2 2026; scale — 2.96M members, one of the largest pure-play ACA carriers, gaining share as larger rivals retreat; member brand/engagement plus ICHRA and +Oscar optionality.
- AGAINST: premiums are filed a year in advance and the ACA 80% minimum MLR caps underwriting margin by law — FY2025's mispricing could not be corrected in-year (MLR 87.4%); risk adjustment transfers ~18.5% of direct premiums away from its younger/healthier pool (FY2025, 10-K) and CMS true-ups arrive late; annual open enrollment means no switching costs; single-market policy exposure (enhanced-subsidy expiry, CMS program-integrity disenrollment of up to ~300k members flagged by management); much larger diversified rivals.
- Evidence check (WORKER_SPEC step 5): fundamentals.json `roic_proxy` is not meaningful for OSCR — its denominator (equity + debt − cash) is negative at a net-cash insurer, so the series swings from −1.519 to +1.259 on sign flips rather than economics. The usable history is operating margin: negative every year 2019–2023, +$57,265,000 on $9,177,564,000 in FY2024, −$396,357,000 on $11,701,427,000 in FY2025, +$629,723,000 TTM. A 3/10 sits on that record; nothing in it supports 7+.
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 5.9 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — engine 5.4 final run (2026-10-19)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's blended growth is −28.91% and g_base floored at −5% — an artifact of the broken revenue tag (BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT), not of the business: filed total revenue grew +27.5% in FY2025 and +42.8% TTM, and FY2026 revenue is guided to $18.7–19.0B. Scenario starts were therefore set by offsets (−0.12 / +0.03 / +0.08 / +0.13 / +0.20 vs the floored g_base) to −10 / −2 / **+3** / +8 / +15%. Every start sits BELOW the recent revenue prints, deliberately: (1) the base being grown is float-inflated OCF, and growing it at premium-growth rates would double-count float; (2) MLR mean-reverts — H1 2026 MLR ~75% was flattered by reserve development, FY2026 is guided to 81–82% with a guided losing H2; (3) 2027 enrollment faces enhanced-subsidy expiry and program-integrity churn. OE multipliers widened on the downside (0.60/0.85) because accrual OE was negative in two of the last three years — a 2025-repeat shrinks even the float base. Probabilities 15/30/30/17/8 widen the bear side per OE_VOLATILE. Price $32.35.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): TTM run and quoted above — and rejected as the base, with the reason in the legs: H1-weighted premium collection (current-YTD OCF $4,711,325,000 vs FY $1,094,854,000) plus +46% membership float makes TTM OE $12.99/share ~7.8× TTM earnings power. The FY-median base is stale but conservative; direction of the staleness is known and it cuts against the stock, not for it.
- **DILUTION** (share count +7.3%/yr): two distinct effects. SBC dollars are FALLING ($159,683,000 → $109,824,000 → $87,654,000 → $75,193,000 TTM) — not SBC runaway. The count growth is (a) pre-IPO/IPO-era history in the CAGR window and (b) a basis effect: FY2025's diluted count (262,388,000) is a loss-year count that excludes dilutive securities, while profitable H1 2026 prints 331,292,000 diluted (ttm.json). The engine base therefore divides by ~26% too few shares on the current diluted basis — one of the quantified supports for the notch below.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in 5 yrs): a tag artifact, not a divestiture or restatement. The engine's revenue tag (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax) captures only "other revenues" ($5,394,000 in 2021 rising to $28,593,000 in 2025); the filer's total revenue (fundamentals.json) grew smoothly: +297% in 2021 is itself the early-scale year off a $462,801,000 base, then +115.6% / +47.9% / +56.5% / +27.5%. No M&A or divestiture break in the window. Consequence: every engine revenue CAGR is garbage and was not used — growth inputs were set from the filed totals and guidance, as documented in the DCF section. Cigna+Oscar wind-down is immaterial (5,168 members at 2025-09-30 vs 2,116,904 total).
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 yrs): real — conservative OE/share ran −$2.06 → +$3.16 → +$3.70 over the last three years and was deeply negative before that. Handled by widening bear-side probability to 45% (15 super bear + 30 bear) and cutting the super-bear multiplier to 0.60.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (>40% in 2024, 2025): structural insurer float, not a one-off. FY2025: net income −$443,151,000 vs OCF +$1,094,854,000; FY2024: +$25,432,000 vs +$978,193,000. The bridge is working capital: ΔNWC −$907,019,000 (2024) and −$878,088,000 (2025) — claims payable, risk-adjustment payable and unearned premiums growing with membership, plus premiums collected ahead of claims. This cash belongs to future claims, not to shareholders, which is precisely why the OCF base overstates distributable OE and why the tier is notched (verdict).
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 5.00x super-bear IV): real — the outcome range for a single-line ACA insurer repricing annually IS this wide. Confidence is low (also capped by the model misfit), and the verdict is sized to the bear end.
- **BIG_NET_CASH** (net cash 2.83x normalized OE): net debt −$2,344,056,000 (cash $2,774,151,000 vs debt $430,095,000, latest FY row). Noted in the verdict with the insurer caveat: most of that cash sits in regulated insurance subsidiaries backing claims liabilities (the Q2 2026 report cited ~$994M of excess surplus in the subs) — it is a solvency buffer, not a distributable pile, so it does not rescue the tier.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear D 9.66% vs bull B 15.80%): verdict sized to the bear end — the final tier is D, at/below the bear case, after the insurer notch.

## Sector model fit — the notch
The engine did not emit SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (the universe classifies OSCR as Health Care; the flag covers Finance/Real Estate/Utilities), but economically Oscar is an insurer and the failure mode is the flagged one: the OCF base capitalizes float. Per the standing policy for insurer misfits (Andrew, 2026-10-15), the final tier is sized one notch down from the numbers tier, with the payable-earnings figure it rests on: an accrual base built only from financials_history.csv figures — net income + D&A − capex per share (SBC is already expensed inside net income, so it is not deducted twice) — is −$1.20 (2023), +$0.11 (2024) and −$1.72 (2025), a last-3 median of **−$1.20/share against the engine's +$3.16 OCF base**. FY2026 guidance ($600–800M operating earnings) says the accrual base is turning positive now, which is why the notch is one tier and not a collapse to F — but a base that was negative on earnings for two of the last three years cannot carry a C on float arithmetic. One generated-field consequence to note: because the flag never fired, make_score.py derives `model_fit: "modeled"` in score.json (it keys solely off the flag) — the misfit assessment for this name lives in this section, the tier_override and the registry, not in that field.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range: accrual-earnings basis → no positive normalized base (F mechanics); engine OCF median base → C (12.13% weighted IRR); TTM OCF basis → an absurd $12.99/share base that would print a fake high tier and was rejected on its legs. The published D sits one notch under the engine's C, per the insurer policy.
- What would change the answer: a full FY2026 audited year at the guided $600–800M operating earnings with MLR at 81–82%, followed by a 2027 that survives the subsidy/program-integrity reset — two clean accrual years would rebuild the median base on earnings instead of float. Until then the earnings base is one good half (flattered by $164M of Q2 reserve development) against a long loss history.
- Balance sheet is not the risk: net cash $2,344,056,000 and no dividend; the risk is underwriting — one bad risk-adjustment true-up erased a full year in 2025, and pricing is locked a year ahead.
- Margin of safety: even on the engine's own float-flattered numbers, the weighted IV@15% of $24.88 sits 23.1% BELOW the $32.35 price — the market has already paid for the 2026 inflection. The bear-case IV@15% is $18.80.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (tier by numbers C at weighted IRR 12.13%, softened one notch for the insurer-float base; bear case independently prints D at 9.66%)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector model misfit in substance, WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD 5.00x, TTM rejected, base divides by a loss-year share count)
- One-liner: ACA health insurer in a real 2026 earnings inflection, moat 3/10 — engine prints Tier C (weighted IRR 12.13%, IV@15% $24.88 vs $32.35) on an OCF base that capitalizes premium float, so the final tier is softened to D at low confidence; on accrual earnings the last-3 median base is negative, and it clears 15% only below ~$24.88 even on engine numbers.
